items.title: Anthropic C.E.O. Dario Amodei Calls for A.I. Slowdown
items.author: Mike Isaac
items.content: <article>In an essay, the head of Anthropic laid out the rapidly advancing capabilities of artificial intelligence and said there needed to be greater safety controls across the industry.</article>

items.title: Why It’s Difficult for Tech Companies to Rein In A.I.
items.author: Sheera Frenkel and Dylan Freedman
items.content: <article>Researchers say artificial intelligence is developing faster than the systems put in place to monitor and control it.</article>

items.title: Inside the Discussions at AI Companies Over a Superintelligence Doomsday
items.author: Mike Isaac and Kate Conger
items.content: <article>Researchers at Anthropic, OpenAI, Meta and Google are increasingly trying to raise awareness about the risks of artificial intelligence.</article>

items.title: California’s Governor Signs Landmark Online Child Safety Bills
items.author: Cecilia Kang and Laurel Rosenhall
items.content: <article>Gov. Gavin Newsom signed a bill that prohibits social media platforms from providing addictive features to users under 16, the first law of its kind in the nation.</article>

items.title: How Amazon’s Zoox Is Taking On Waymo in San Francisco
items.author: Emmy Martin
items.content: <article>The Amazon-owned driverless car company is a distant second to Waymo. Its pitch to riders? Wine pop-ups, festival sponsorships and a car built to be filmed.</article>

items.title: How the New iPhone Duo’s Glass Screen Bends Without Breaking
items.author: William J. Broad
items.content: <article>The screens of foldable phones are a triumph of materials science and microengineering.</article>

items.title: How Minnesota Became the Front Line in the Fight Over Prediction Markets
items.author: Lauren McCarthy
items.content: <article>The state was the first to pass a law banning Kalshi and Polymarket. A lawsuit filed by a federal agency may set a precedent on who gets to regulate them.</article>

items.title: The Mic Is On. So Is Live Auto-Tune.
items.author: Malia Mendez
items.content: <article>As audiences demand perfection from live performances, pitch correction technology has become an increasingly common way for singers to deliver.</article>

items.title: Could A.I. Really Kill All Humans?
items.content: <article>After an Anthropic researcher quit, warning that the A.I. race is “gambling with our lives,” Cade Metz joined Natalie Kitroeff on “The Call” to break down what’s at stake.</article>

items.title: Elon Musk Has Pledged to Rid His Platform, X, of Child Sexual Abuse, but It Persists
items.author: Kate Conger and Michael H. Keller
items.content: <article>Reviews by the Canadian Center for Child Protection and The New York Times found that explicit images of children remain on the social media site owned by Elon Musk.</article>

items.title: The Ezra Klein Show: The A.I. Revolt Is Here
items.author: Ezra Klein and Rollin Hu
items.content: <article>The A.I. giants weren’t prepared for this.</article>

items.title: Anthropic Says It Blocked Possible Efforts to Build Biological Weapons
items.author: Dustin Volz
items.content: <article>In a new report, the A.I. start-up added that it could not determine whether the research was legitimate or nefarious, leading the company to shut down the work.</article>

items.title: Why is Apple’s New Foldable iPhone Duo $1,999?
items.author: Brian X. Chen
items.content: <article>The company unveiled a new iPhone that costs $1,999. Here are the economics behind that price tag.</article>

items.title: Anthropic Researchers Raise Alarm Over A.I. Acceleration, Warning of Threat to Humanity
items.author: Kate Conger
items.content: <article>Their warnings echo concerns that other artificial intelligence experts have voiced in recent months, as calls increase for a slowdown in the pace of development.</article>

items.title: Apple Unveils the iPhone Duo, a Foldable Phone That Costs $1,999
items.author: Kalley Huang
items.content: <article>At the company’s annual September product event, Apple also demonstrated its work on artificial intelligence and other new devices.</article>

items.title: Why California Is Reconsidering Its Decision to Shun Nuclear Power
items.author: Ivan Penn and Adam Perez
items.content: <article>The state is considering extending the life of its last nuclear power plant, Diablo Canyon, and allowing construction of new reactors to help meet its clean energy goals.</article>

items.title: Meta Introduces Muse, an A.I. Agent That Can Send Your Emails and Book Your Travel
items.author: Eli Tan
items.content: <article>Muse, Meta’s new A.I. agent, acts as a personal digital assistant that connects to Facebook and Instagram, as well as third-party apps such as Spotify and OpenTable.</article>

items.title: A Hacking Tool Built With A.I. Can Breach Phones Without a Click
items.author: Dustin Volz
items.content: <article>An attack discovered by A.I. researchers could have compromised hundreds of millions of devices within hours, experts said.</article>

items.title: Apple Expected to Unveil a Folding iPhone at Annual Launch Event
items.author: Kalley Huang
items.content: <article>Fans of the company’s products widely believe it will unveil a folding smartphone at its annual launch event on Wednesday.</article>

items.title: Key App Developers Have Yet to Embrace Apple’s New Siri A.I.
items.author: Kalley Huang and Brian X. Chen
items.content: <article>For the company’s new artificial intelligence system to take off, it will need plenty of support from the makers of popular apps on Apple’s phones.</article>

items.title: Virtual Taekwondo Takes the Contact Out of a Combat Sport
items.author: Yan Zhuang and Jean Chung
items.content: <article>The contactless version of the Korean martial art is making its debut at this year’s Asian Games. Critics say it’s a glorified video game.</article>

items.title: How a Blacklisted Chinese Tech Giant Kept Buying America’s Best A.I. Chips
items.author: Ana Swanson, Paul Mozur, Tripp Mickle and Keith Bradsher
items.content: <article>Washington imposed sanctions on Inspur because of its work with the Chinese military. But the company’s subsidiary kept shipping Nvidia’s best chips to feed China’s leading A.I. firms.</article>

items.title: Early Data Indicates an A.I.-Generated Drug Could Slow Aging
items.author: Cade Metz
items.content: <article>Artificial intelligence was used to help develop a drug candidate, rentosertib, for a rare lung condition. Its maker says the drug also seems to reduce the biological hallmarks of age.</article>
